recipes.name: Cranberry Oatmeal Cookies
ingredients_raw: 1 cup unsalted butter at room temperature

steps.text: Preheat the oven to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C). Place an oven rack in the upper third of the oven. Line baking sheets with parchment paper.

Place unsalted butter and light brown sugar into the work bowl of a stand mixer and mix on medium-slow speed until very fluffy, 3 to 4 minutes. Beat in vanilla extract, followed by eggs, one at a time. Reduce mixer speed to lowest speed and leave running.

Whisk rolled oats, flour, baking powder, cinnamon, kosher salt, and nutmeg together in a separate bowl; gradually add oat mixture into the slowly running mixer, a 1/3 at a time. Mix in dried cranberries and nuts until just incorporated. Using a large cookie scoop, place dough on prepared baking sheet about 2 inches apart.
Bake one batch at a time in the preheated oven just until the edges are brown, 15 to 18 minutes. Allow to cool briefly on baking sheets before removing to finish cooling on wire racks.

raw_recipe.headline: Cranberry Oatmeal Cookies
raw_recipe.description: These chewy oatmeal cranberry cookies with dried cranberries and pecans are a perfect festive treat and a great addition to any holiday cookie platter.

review.reviewBody: I overcooked my first batch at 16 minutes, and they rose up, didn't spread out. Finished the rest at 14 minutes, and flattened slightly before going into the oven. Just a little salty for me, so I'll cut that back to 1 tsp the next time. Good combination of flavors yielding soft-textured cookies.

I only used a pinch of salt, based on others' reviews of it being too salty. And I substituted goji berries for cranberries, because that was all I had on hand. (Next time would use cranberries and walnuts, I think.) Put in one baking sheet at a time, turned it after 10 minutes and then baked for another five. They were perfect.

3/16/19 - substituted whole wheat flour for all purpose. Reduced flour to 1 1/4 cups and supplemented with 1/4 cup of oat bran and flax seed. Used turbinado sugar and reduced by 1/4 cup. Reduced salt by 1/2 tsp. Subbed raisins and walnuts. Subbed 1/4 tsp of ginger and reduced cinnamon to 1/4 tsp. Cooked 20 mins. Crunchier cookie and very wholesome flavor. Sunflower seeds would be a nice addition.
Cookies are very good! I did make a couple of changes: I used only 1/2 tsp salt and baked for 9 minutes.
The cookies were good. I decreased the salt to ¾ teaspoon as recommended by another reviewer. The recipe didn't take 18 minutes. So, watch the cookies around 15 minutes and check for doneness.

This recipe was very good. The only thing I did different was add WAY less salt (about half a teaspoon) and I could really taste the salt in the finished product but it was *just* right. I also added white chocolate chips and cooked for 16 minutes on an insulated cookie sheet with parchment paper before removing and placing on a cooling rack. Next time I will add a little more cinnamon and I think they would be perfect!

Used 1/4 c. Almond flour; 1/4 c. Whole wheat flour; 1/2 c. Oat flour & 1/2 c. Plain flour.

Added 1/2 c. 60% Ghirardelli chocolate chips.
Baked for 16 min., @ 325 degrees, convection oven, 2 racks from top of oven.

Delicious!!!!

Excellent cookie recipe! I did add 1/2 c. White chocolate chips. Definitely decrease the salt. I used just about 1 tsp. And next time I’ll use 1/2-3/4 tsp. For a bit more nutrition I used 1C. Whole wheat flour and 1/2 c. White flour. I added a bit more cinnamon too. This one’s a keeper. Rave reviews from my cookie monsters.
Taste great. Watch baking time. Recipe calls for 17-18 minutes but I bake the batch at 8 minutes. Also, salt to taste, so try first batch using 1 tsp.

The house smells wonderful and the cookies are delicious. I did cut the salt down to 1t, and flattened them just a little. I left the oven rack in the center and cooked 12-13 minutes, and followed the 5 minute rest before moving to the cooling rack. Very good.

I made these cookies to bring to a German kids club meetup and everyone loved them. They were definitely a bit on the salty side as other reviewers mentioned, so next time I would cut the salt in half. I used macadamia nuts instead of pecans because I am allergic to pecans and they were so delicious. I ate them as a snack and for breakfast the following two days and they stayed soft and perfect when covered airtight at room temperature. A note for when you’re baking them: The first batch I baked using 2 baking trays, which I rotated half way through baking. The cookies did not spread as much. The second batch was enough for one more tray and they spread more baking on the middle rack, resulting in a more desirable, traditional cookie shape.
1st time: added white chocolate ate chips - betcha can't eat just one! 2nd time: traded out the pecans for toasted pine nuts and the cranberries for dried dates - also scrumptious.
Amazing base recipe. I am not an Oatmeal Cookie person, but this recipe with some Ghiardelli White chocolate chips added was AMAZING. I think I may like Oatmeal cookies now.
The only change I made was cut the salt by half and it was great.
Easy to follow and great taste!
The toasted pecans and nutmeg kick this recipe up a notch. Made these last year to use up cranberries, but they are now in the rotation. Tonight they will be a hostess gift.
Very good. Instead of pecans I added more cranberries.
These are great! Everyone loved them! I did NOT add any salt tho and im glad. The only thing is I wish they were moister. But I will be making these again!
Absolutely delicious! Crispy bottoms and chewy centers. Toasted pecans are a bonus.
I used self rising flour and added a cup of chocolate chips! Best cookie ever as reported by my family!
